:::{#def-convex-set}
#### Convex set

A set $K \subseteq \reals^p$ is **convex** if for all $\vx, \vy \in K$ and all $t \in [0, 1]$,
the point $t \vx + (1 - t) \vy$ is in $K$:
$K$ contains the whole line segment between any two of its points.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-convex-set}
#### Convex sets

- $\reals^p$ is convex, and so is any set with at most one point.
- The closed ball $B = \cb{\vx : \norm{\vx} \le r}$ is convex:
  for $\vx, \vy \in B$ and $t \in [0, 1]$,

  $$
  \ba
  \norm{t \vx + (1 - t) \vy}
  &\le \norm{t \vx} + \norm{(1 - t) \vy}
  && \text{(triangle inequality)}
  \\
  &= t\,\norm{\vx} + (1 - t)\,\norm{\vy}
  && \text{(} t \ge 0 \text{ and } 1 - t \ge 0 \text{)}
  \\
  &\le t\,r + (1 - t)\,r
  && \text{(} \vx, \vy \in B \text{)}
  \\
  &= r.
  && \text{(arithmetic)}
  \ea
  $$

  The first step is the [triangle inequality](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-triangle-inequality),
  and the second uses [the norm of a multiple](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-norm-properties).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-convex-set}
#### A set that is not convex

$K = \cb{x \in \reals : \abs{x} \ge 1}$ is not convex:
$-1$ and $1$ are in $K$,
but with $t = \tfrac{1}{2}$ the point $\tfrac{1}{2}(-1) + \tfrac{1}{2}(1) = 0$ is not.

:::
